subject: Post-call: Multilingual model evals & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@globexretail.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@globexretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-call: Multilingual model evals & next steps

Thanks for the time today, Aisha and Tom — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Summary of ask:
- Globex wants parity in customer-facing NLU/generation across EU locales (EN, FR, DE, ES) and APAC priority languages (JA, KO). Primary KPIs: accuracy of slot extraction, locale-specific fluency, and hallucination reduction for policy-critical responses.

2) Model fit / quick recommendations (initial):
- For lower-latency production: redwood-multilingual-v1 (quantized) for templated responses + locale-specific prompt templates.
- For high-quality generation (long-form & nuanced locales): redwood-multilingual-large / redwood-multilingual-xt. Use the larger variant for German long-form where we saw regression risk.
- Fallback policy: smaller model + cached canonical responses for high-SLA flows.

3) Evals we discussed today (deliverables):
- We will run a 5k-prompt per-locale automated eval (BLEU/chrF + Rouge) and a 500-sample human review focused on hallucination/brand safety per locale.
- Share prompt sets and benchmark scripts via Drive.

4) Risks / immediate concerns:
- We saw a potential quality regression on DE long-form responses in earlier benchmarks; will prioritize a targeted pass.
- Tokenization differences and date/number formatting in FR/DE may need locale-specific post-processing.

5) Ownership & next steps:
- Neha: run the per-locale automated evals and push results to the Drive folder by 2027-05-10.
- Marissa: coordinate a follow-up call and send access to prompt sets today.
- Aisha/Tom: confirm target locales and any customer-specific test cases by EOD 2027-05-04.

Attachments: I uploaded the prompt set CSV and a short eval summary PDF to the Drive folder and attached stubs to this thread.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@globexretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@globexretail.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 17:48:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Multilingual model evals & next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed locales: EN, FR, DE, ES for EU phase 1. APAC: JA and KO as phase 2.
- We will share 3 customer-specific test cases (returns, warranty FAQ, cross-border shipping) by EOD 2027-05-04.
- Attachment: I uploaded our internal sample prompts (customer_cases_globex.xlsx) to the Drive link you shared. Please include the sample set in the 500 human-review queue.

One ask on evaluation metrics: In addition to BLEU/chrF, can Redwood include an intent-match metric for slot extraction and a hallucination rate (false facts per 100 replies)? Those are what our CS team cares about.

If possible, can you also call out any locale-specific tokenization or normalization transforms you will apply so we can mirror them in our data?

Best,
Aisha

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@globexretail.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@globexretail.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call: Multilingual model evals & next steps

Adding a few technical notes so expectations are aligned: 

- Eval plan: automated pass will compute BLEU/chrF + intent-match (via our slot-F1 script) + hallucination proxy (entity drift and phrase novelty score). Human review rubric will annotate hallucination severity and fluency per locale.
- Locale-specific processing: for FR/DE we will apply locale-normalization (unicode NFKC, currency/date canonicalization, number grouping) and a language-specific tokenizer before scoring. Japanese/Korean will use language-specific tokenizers and character-level chrF.
- Model config: we will test two quantization profiles — q4_0 (faster) and q8_0 (higher quality) — to see tradeoffs. Also plan one run with extended context (8k) for DE long-form scenarios.
- Regression detection: for each locale we will compute delta vs baseline across key metrics and flag regressions >3% absolute drop or hallucination increase >0.5 per 100 replies.

I'll start the automated runs tonight and aim to post preliminary dashboards to the Drive folder by 2027-05-10. If we find regressions, recommend a canary rollout to 5% of traffic with automated rollback.

Neha
Lead Applied ML, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@globexretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Multilingual model evals & next steps

Appreciate the quick responses. Short update and firmed timeline: 

- Aisha/Tom: we received your customer test cases and the sample prompts — thanks.
- Neha: thanks — please prioritize DE long-form and provide the first regression report by 2027-05-10.
- Action: I'll schedule a 30-minute follow-up on 2027-05-12 at 10:00 PT to review preliminary results and decide on canary sizing. Invite coming shortly.

Deliverables before follow-up: 
- Automated eval results + per-locale dashboards (Neha)
- Human review sample highlights (Neha)
- A short slide (Marissa) summarizing recommended model variant and rollout plan (attached).

If anything changes, flag in the Drive folder and ping me.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

--
Marissa
